傳奇圖像設計師 Susan Kare recently attended the Startup School 2026 event, and her talk is now available on Y Combinator's YouTube channel. Please see the video below.

Susan Kare shares fascinating stories and design insights

It's been over 40 years since the original Macintosh debuted, and the system's graphics, fonts, icons, and overall UI elements still look fresh today, just as they did back then.

In fact, many of the elements Susan Kare designed for the original Macintosh still appear in macOS today, preserved either in spirit or quite literally. From the Command key symbol, the "Happy Mac" startup icon, and the system font to the hand cursor and more, Kare's work not only shaped the Mac's visual language but also influenced the entire personal computer industry.

While anyone who has studied Apple's history has likely seen Kare's sketches and may have read or heard her interviews about that early work, hearing her speak firsthand about those years filled with passion and frustration is still deeply rewarding — after all, back then, graphical user interfaces and bitmaps were still uncharted territory.

For that reason, if you're interested in design, Apple's history, or simply enjoy hearing experts speak passionately about topics they've devoted their lives to, Kare's talk is an absolute must-watch.

Beyond detailing her work at Apple in depth, Kare also discusses how she came to join the company, showcases her projects after leaving, shares little-known stories from Apple's early days, and quotes other legendary designers to offer extra inspiration.
